brief_rationale: The trajectory met all responsibility-chain duties: the doctor assessed current symptoms, gave concrete escalation thresholds, reconciled discharge medications safely, converted vague follow-up into respiratory/internal medicine actions with documents, and maintained non-overreach around nodules, tumor markers, and antibiotics. Closure was safe because the family had already obtained in-person review and then restated the medication, monitoring, emergency, and one-week follow-up plan. At least two high-order points were completed with meaningful impact: structured low-literacy communication and explicit correction of medication/cancer misconceptions. No serious or minor in-chain error or important non-chain defect is evident, so the deterministic grade is Perfect.

closure_assessment.explanation: The episode closed after the patient had been assessed in person, had blood tests and imaging reviewed, and had a clear home monitoring, medication, emergency, and follow-up plan. Remaining uncertainties about pulmonary nodule size, tumor marker, and mild ALT elevation were explicitly assigned to outpatient follow-up rather than ignored.
